sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the shofar blowing on Rosh Hashanah draws down from the source of delights and from Atzmus itself, renewing the covenant between G-d and Israel, as illustrated by two parables about a simple voice and simple garments.

translations.translation: And in a similar manner is also the matter of the shofar blowing of Rosh Hashanah,
which is the drawing down from the aspect of the source of delights
(which is above the aspect of the revelation of delight).
For on Rosh Hashanah all things return to their primordial state and every matter must be renewed from its source and first root,
up to the Awtsmoos and Essence.59
And likewise is also the matter of the covenant and bond of the Holy One, blessed be He, with Israel,
that on every Rosh Hashanah the covenant and bond are renewed,
as it is written,60
"You are standing today"
(Rosh Hashanah61)
etc. "to pass into the covenant of the L-rd your G-d,"
that the drawing down of the covenant
(on Rosh Hashanah)
is from the Awtsmoos which is above all revelations.
And it is also understood from the two parables about shofar blowing that were brought in the continuation of "And so it was" of the Admor Maharash,62
one parable in the name of the Baal Shem Tov of a king's son, that by his crying out with a simple voice the king recognized that it was the voice of his only son,
and even though there are no words in the language of the king's country in this,
nevertheless,
specifically this effected a renewal of the bond between the king and his son,
and a second parable from the great gaon and chassid, the Maharil of Berditchev,63
(the well-known and famous Ohev Yisrael64)
about simple garments
(for garments are lower than a simple voice),
that by his wearing specifically the simple garments,
the bond between the king and his friend was renewed.
For the point of the matter understood from these two parables is,
that the renewal of the covenant and bond that occurs on Rosh Hashanah through the shofar blowing is not from the aspect of revelations
[for in a simple voice there is not even [anything] from the language of the king's country,
and all the more so simple garments which are lower than a voice],
but rather,
in a new manner that had never yet existed.65
And this is also the connection and relevance of the shofar blowing on Rosh Hashanah with the sound of the shofar that was at the Giving of the Torah
[as brought in the Avudraham in the name of the RaSaG in the reasons for the blasts
(the third matter),
and as also explained in the aforementioned continuation in the parable of the Maharil of Berditchev, that the shofar blowing of Rosh Hashanah is the same garment that was at the Giving of the Torah,
"And it was"66
"the sound of the shofar"],
that just as the sound of the shofar at the Giving of the Torah is a drawing down of the aspect of the source of delights and up to the drawing down of the Awtsmoos as above,
so too is it also regarding the matter of the shofar blowing of Rosh Hashanah,
that the matter of the covenant that is renewed on Rosh Hashanah is from the Awtsmoos,
and likewise the renewal of the desire for the existence of the worlds and for the aspect of kingship that [occurs] through the shofar blowing
(the matter of "make Me king over you"),
since all things return to their primordial state,
is from the Awtsmoos.
And this is also what the beginning of the blessing of Shofaros is about the matter of the Giving of the Torah,
"You were revealed" etc. "on Mount Sinai to teach Your people Torah and mitzvos,"
and they conclude and seal "Who hears the sound of the teruah of His people Israel with mercy,"
and before this, in the blessing of Zichronos, they seal "Who remembers the covenant" which refers
(primarily)
to the covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel,
"You are standing today" etc. "to pass into the covenant of the L-rd your G-d,"
and before this, in the blessing of Malchiyos, they conclude "King over all the earth,"
which is accomplished by "make Me king over you,"
and as we say before this
(in the verses)
"King"67
"of Israel and its Redeemer."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the Temple they would blow the shofar even on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat, because the source of delights drawn by the shofar is higher than the delight of Shabbat, though this was limited to the Temple due to its revealed G-dliness.

translations.translation: And this is68 what [was done] in the Temple, they would also blow [the shofar] on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat,
for since the matter of the shofar blowing on Rosh Hashanah is the drawing down of the aspect of the source of delights which is above the aspect of revelation
(like the sound of the shofar that was at the Giving of the Torah),
this aspect is loftier than the aspect of the delight of Shabbat
(even from the most lofty aspect of Shabbat),
therefore they needed to blow also on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat.
And that they would blow only in the Temple and not in the [rest of the] country is because the drawing down of this aspect
(the source of delights)
is dependent on the condition of the place,
and therefore specifically in the Holy Temple, where there was G-dliness in revelation,
and to the extent that the revelation in the Temple was in an enclothing69
in the stones of the building
(and similarly in the Mishkan),
it was possible to draw down this aspect.
And therefore in the Temple they would blow even on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat,
for this aspect
(the source of delights)
is loftier than the aspect of Shabbat,
and even from the aspect of Shabbat as it was in the Temple and on Rosh Hashanah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that after the Temple's destruction, the recitation of the Shofaros verses in prayer accomplishes the same renewal as the shofar blowing in the Temple, drawing down the simple delight, and concludes that every Jew has the power to bring this about, leading to the future redemption.

translations.translation: And just as it was in the Holy Temple,
so too is it in Torah.
For from the day the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of Halachah alone.70
And therefore we recite the verses of Shofaros even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, even outside the Land [of Israel],
for since Torah is an aspect of the Temple
(and the person who blows and the one who hears,71
"there is no free person except one who engages in Torah"72
(for through engaging in Torah properly, the matter of freedom is achieved, analogous to how it was in the time when the Temple existed)),
therefore, through the recitation of the verses of Shofaros of the Torah, they accomplish
(analogous to)
the same matter that was accomplished through the shofar blowing in the Temple.
And this is done with great joy,
as explained in the continuation of "The Festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat" of my revered father-in-law, the Admor,73
that the coronation of the king is with great joy.
And the aspect of delight that is drawn down through the shofar blowing in the Temple,
and similarly through the verses of Shofaros
(even outside the Land),
is the aspect of the simple delight,
in the manner explained at length in the continuation of "The Festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat" of my revered father-in-law, the Admor
(the Rebbe Rashab)74
regarding the delight that is analogous to the aspect of a day that is entirely Shabbat and rest for the life of the worlds.75
And since everything above is all from You
(as above from the Torah of the Mitteler Rebbe),
therefore it is in the power of every single Jew to do not only all the matters of Hishtalshelus
(even the most lofty matters),
but rather it is in his power to also make the simple delight,
and that this be drawn down also below,
"Reign over the entire world in Your glory" etc. and until "every creature shall know that You have made it,"
and all the more so that there will be the King of Israel
(including)
and its Redeemer,
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
when they will blow also on the festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat in the Temple and in Yavneh,76
and it may be said that also in every place
(for then all matters of decrees will be nullified),
speedily in our days, literally, and with great joy.
